title: Warm-Up Saturday
source: Midnight Bet — Integrated ARC II — Games People Play
paragraphs: Saturday did not become the final game. Kabir tried. Rhea refused. “Too soon.” Kabir stared. “Too soon for cards?” “For whatever face you are making.” Naina laughed. Mira agreed. “Warm-up only.” Dev looked relieved. Aarav pretended not to. They met at Kabir’s duplex at eight. Same place final game would eventually happen. Tonight was rehearsal. Food first. Music. Old stories. Then simple games. No overnight rule. Kabir had written overnight in the invite; Rhea vetoed it before dinner, and he dropped the rule.

No dramatic stakes. Still the erotic baseline came with them. Aarav arrived after seeing Ananya. Not a class. Coffee. Public café. Their first meeting outside her studio. Mira knew. Not details. Enough. When Aarav entered, Mira looked at him. The soft upper curves of her breasts were clear under the thin top she wore. Her eyes moved over him the same way they had on the rooftop — thorough, deliberate. “Teacher?” He smiled.

“Coach.” “Same thing.” “She hates that.” Mira’s jealousy warmed. Heat settled low in her stomach at the thought of Ananya wanting him enough to meet outside the studio, Ananya’s voice telling him to look at her, Ananya’s body close enough that he had obeyed without thinking. “Good.” Kabir arrived from Meera’s session. Rhea noticed his mouth before she hated herself for it — the faint memory of another woman’s lipstick, the quiet satisfaction that sat under his smile.

“Meera?” Kabir grinned. “Statistics.” “Your statistics look happy.” He laughed. The memory of Meera’s soft mouth against his, the way she had said “yes” and then told him to go to rehearsal, still sat under his skin. Dev came last. Shalini had texted him: Enjoy your night. Do not retreat. Naina saw the message preview. She smiled.

“Hot.” Dev locked phone. “Boundary.” “Coward.” The first game was ordinary cards. No penalties. Sana and Mehul joined for the first hour. Tara and Rohan stopped by with leftover wedding food. Neha and Arjun came to return speakers. The house filled beyond six. Exactly what the rewrite needed. One connected social life. Sana sat beside Aarav. The soft press of her thigh against his when she shifted was deliberate enough to notice.

Mira noticed. Mehul sat beside Mira. His knee brushed hers under the table. Warm. Steady. Different from Aarav’s. Aarav noticed. Tara leaned against the kitchen counter near Kabir. The soft curve of her hip against the edge of the counter. The thin fabric of her top shifting when she breathed. Rhea noticed. Arjun asked Rhea about guest rooms. His voice low. His eyes dropping once to the open neckline of her top before returning to her face.

Kabir noticed. Shalini’s name appeared again on Dev’s phone. Naina noticed. Nobody had to manufacture heat. It entered with seating. Sana suggested a game. “Two truths.” Kabir groaned. “Boring.” “Make it adult.” Rhea looked suspicious. “How?” Sana smiled. “Two truths.”

“One desire.” Silence. Mehul looked at his wife. “Of course.” The rules stayed non-explicit. No naming if unwanted. No forced detail. Just one thing a person wanted recently. Mira went first. Truth: She hated pineapple pizza. Truth: She had lied to someone this week. Desire:

“To be looked at without pretending I do not notice.” The room quieted. Aarav looked at her. Mehul did too. Both pairs of eyes moved over her body — the soft shape of her breasts under the thin top, the narrow waist, the way her legs crossed under the table. Mira smiled. “Next.” Aarav’s turn. Truth: He had skipped gym twice. Truth: He had wanted to kiss someone outside the friend circle recently. Mira’s face changed. The knowledge that Ananya was no longer only his coach sat between them like heat.

Everyone else reacted. Kabir shouted. “What?” Aarav looked at Mira. Then away. No name. Desire: “To stop having to choose between honesty and peace.” Sana smiled. Naina looked thoughtful. Mira drank water. The jealousy was physical now — a low ache between her legs that made her shift in her seat. Kabir’s turn. Truth: He had lied to Rhea about being jealous. Truth: He had kissed someone this week who was not Rhea. Rhea stared.

Meera. She knew. Still hearing it hurt. The memory of Kabir’s mouth against hers in the parking basement mixed with the knowledge that another woman had tasted him since. Desire: “To kiss someone I should not.” Tara’s eyes moved. Rohan was in the kitchen. Rhea saw Tara move. Kabir saw Rhea see. Danger multiplied. The soft press of Tara’s hand on his chest the night before returned to his skin like a brand. Rhea’s turn.

Truth: She had thought about Arjun. Silence. Neha was not in the room. Arjun was. Everyone froze. Rhea corrected: “In an inappropriate way.” Arjun’s jaw tightened. The memory of his hand at her waist during the sangeet, the soft press of her breast against his chest when she leaned in, the quiet admission that he wanted to kiss her — all of it sat between them. Kabir looked at him. Truth two: She had kissed someone in the group.

Now everyone exploded. Kabir covered his face. Naina screamed. Mira stared. Aarav laughed. Rhea smiled. No name. Desire: “To stop answering questions now.” Everyone laughed. Tension saved by humour. But the heat remained. Dev’s turn. Truth: He had kissed someone outside the group. Naina’s eyes flashed. Shalini. The soft press of Shalini’s mouth against his, the way her body had leaned into the second kiss, the deliberate nearness she had chosen.

Truth: He liked being told what to do by one specific woman. Naina smiled. Shalini. Desire: “To find out whether I like control or just trust.” The room went quiet. Naina looked at him differently. Her turn. Truth: She had kissed someone in the group. Dev looked down. Truth: She had imagined kissing someone married. Mehul’s eyebrows lifted. Sana smiled. Aarav looked surprised. Desire: “To know if jealousy can make something hotter without making it ugly.”

Sana clapped once. “Good answer.” Mehul looked at his wife. Interesting. The game had not touched anyone. Still the room felt charged. Rohan returned from the kitchen. Tara looked normal. Kabir did not. The memory of her hand on his chest, her quiet “yes” to wanting, her “not now” that still left the door open — all of it sat under his skin. Arjun left early with Neha’s call. Rhea watched him go. The soft line of his shoulders under the shirt. The way he had looked at her on the balcony when he admitted he wanted to kiss her.

Kabir saw. Sana and Mehul stayed longer. Sana sat beside Naina. Whispered something. Naina laughed. Mehul stood with Mira near the balcony. His body close enough that the heat of him reached her. The soft scent of his cologne. The quiet knowledge that his wife knew and still stayed. Aarav’s jealousy returned.

The next game was simpler. Guess the song. Loser changed seat. Nothing sexual. Seat changes created everything. Round one. Mira lost. Moved beside Dev. Aarav watched. Naina watched too. Mira’s knee touched Dev’s. Neither moved immediately. The warm pressure of her thigh against his stayed deliberate. Dev smiled. Mira smiled back. Aarav’s face hardened. Round two. Rhea lost. Moved beside Aarav. Kabir stared. Rhea sat close.

Too close. The soft press of her breast against his arm when she shifted was clear through the thin fabric of her top. Aarav noticed. Rhea whispered: “Manage?” He laughed. “Barely.” Kabir saw the laugh. Jealousy sharpened. Round three. Naina lost. Moved beside Kabir. Rhea’s eyes narrowed. Dev’s too. Naina leaned back. The soft curve of her body against the sofa. The short dress riding higher on her thighs.

“Hello.” Kabir smiled. “Danger.” “Original.” The game continued. Every seat change built cross-pair familiarity. Sana watched like an event planner studying flow. Mehul watched like a man discovering his wife enjoyed the same chaos he did. At ten, Tara and Rohan left. Tara hugged Rhea. Then Kabir. Her hand at his back — soft fingers spreading against the fabric of his shirt, the same place she had touched his chest the night before.

Rhea saw. Kabir stayed still. Tara whispered: “Behave.” Kabir smiled. Rhea heard only tone. Enough. At ten-thirty, Sana and Mehul left. Sana hugged Aarav. The soft press of her body against his for one full second longer than necessary. Mira saw. Mehul hugged Naina casually. His hand at her waist for a beat too long. Dev saw. Marriage couple exited holding hands. That visual mattered. They could desire outside and still return together.

The six remained. Now the room shifted. Less audience. More history. Kabir reached for the card deck. Rhea slapped his hand. “No final game.” Kabir groaned. Mira said: “One warm-up.” Naina smiled. “Eye contact.” Dev sighed. Of course. Pairs random. First: Mira–Kabir. Rhea froze. Aarav did too. Thirty seconds. At five they laughed. At fifteen Mira noticed serious Kabir — the same quiet intensity he showed when he stopped joking around Tara or Meera.

At twenty Kabir noticed Mira’s eyes drop once — to his mouth, to the open collar of his shirt, to the place where another woman’s lipstick had been. At twenty-five both stopped smiling. Thirty. They looked away. Rhea’s heartbeat had changed. Aarav’s too. Second: Rhea–Dev. Kabir stared. Naina watched. Rhea and Dev knew their trust track already. Eye contact made it visible — the quiet way Dev held her gaze, the soft line of her mouth when she did not look away.

Thirty seconds ended quietly. Third: Naina–Aarav. Mira crossed her arms. Dev leaned back. Naina smiled at Aarav. He smiled back. Easy chemistry. The soft shape of her breasts under the short dress. The way her legs crossed when she sat closer. Thirty seconds felt natural. That made both observers more jealous. Then primary pairs. Mira–Aarav. Rhea–Kabir. Naina–Dev. The room became heavier. Mira and Aarav remembered rooftop — the soft give of her body when he held her waist, the taste of her mouth, the way she had said “later.”

Rhea and Kabir remembered parking — the rain, the damp shirt, the slow second kiss, the way her hands had moved into his hair. Naina and Dev remembered balcony — the first quiet kiss, the second longer one, the way she had told him not to retreat. No one knew all three. The timer ended. No kiss. Warm-up only. At eleven, everyone left. Kabir stood alone in the living room. Looked at the deck. Final game still ahead. Tonight had proven something.
It would not need to create heat. It would only need to remove excuses.
Sunday would prove that the women outside the core six had already changed how the six behaved inside it.
